candidate_relations.scope_detail: Pierre Robin facial component missing femoral-facial syndrome

candidate_relations.reason: Abruptio-related growth restriction is an obstetric contributor to SGA, not femoral-facial syndrome.
Cleft lip and palate syndrome captures one malformation and omits femoral aplasia/hypoplasia and unusual facies.
Fetal akinesia deformation sequence is a different hypomotility phenotype.
Amniotic band syndrome is a disruptive sequence not matching bilateral femoral deficiency plus facies.
Prenatal growth restriction is a biometric finding, not the malformation syndrome.
Jarcho-Levin syndrome is a spondylocostal dysplasia, not femoral-facial syndrome.
Abruptio placentae is a pregnancy complication associated with the delivery, not the congenital syndrome.
A small patent ductus arteriosus is an associated cardiac finding, not femoral-facial syndrome.
Congenital malformations is a nonspecific parent missing femoral-facial syndrome.
Oligohydramnios sequence may contribute to deformation but does not constitute femoral-facial syndrome.
Limb abnormalities name the femoral deficiency without the unusual facies/cleft composite.
Osteogenesis imperfecta is a bone-fragility dysplasia, not femoral aplasia with unusual facies.
Fibular aplasia–complex brachydactyly is a related limb-deficiency syndrome with incompatible fibular rather than femoral focus.
Skeletal dysplasia is a parent category omitting femoral-facial syndrome.
Femoral hypoplasia-unusual facies syndrome is the established synonym of femoral-facial syndrome.
Osteochondrodysplasia is a broad skeletal-dysplasia parent without FFS specificity.
Abruptio placentae sequence is obstetric context, not the malformation diagnosis.
Limb-body wall complex is a different disruptive body-wall anomaly.
Craniofacial abnormalities omit the defining femoral aplasia/hypoplasia.
